.NET, Python & Node.JS Clients

1. .NET Thin Client
  • Install via NuGet: Apache.Ignite
  • var cfg = new IgniteClientConfiguration
{
    Endpoints = new[] { "192.168.1.10:10800" },
    EnablePartitionAwareness = true
};

using var client = Ignition.StartClient(cfg);
var cache = client.GetOrCreateCache<int, string>("myCache");

cache.Put(1, "Alice");
string value = cache.Get(1);
  • Supports key-value, SQL, transactions, and binary objects;
2. Python Thin Client
  • Install: pip install pyignite
  • from pyignite import Client

client = Client()
client.connect('192.168.1.10', 10800)

cache = client.get_or_create_cache('myCache')
cache.put(1, 'Alice')
value = cache.get(1)

# SQL queries
result = client.sql('SELECT * FROM Person WHERE age > ?', query_args=[25])
for row in result:
    print(row)
  • Supports key-value, SQL queries, and partition awareness;
3. Node.JS Thin Client
  • Install: npm install apache-ignite-client
  • const IgniteClient = require('apache-ignite-client');
const IgniteClientConfiguration = IgniteClient.IgniteClientConfiguration;

const client = new IgniteClient();
const config = new IgniteClientConfiguration('192.168.1.10:10800');

await client.connect(config);

const cache = await client.getOrCreateCache('myCache');
await cache.put(1, 'Alice');
const value = await cache.get(1);
4. C++ Thin Client
  • Included in the Ignite binary distribution under platforms/cpp/;
  • #include <ignite/thin/ignite_client.h>
#include <ignite/thin/ignite_client_configuration.h>

using namespace ignite::thin;

IgniteClientConfiguration cfg;
cfg.SetEndPoints("192.168.1.10:10800");

IgniteClient client = IgniteClient::Start(cfg);
cache::CacheClient<int, std::string> cache =
    client.GetOrCreateCache<int, std::string>("myCache");

cache.Put(1, "Alice");
std::string value = cache.Get(1);
